slides.title: VMs with one Kubernetes control plane
slides.subtitle: OpenStack comparison / qrab target architecture
slides.notes: Five-minute presentation. The comparison uses the operator-supplied OpenStack topology and inspected qrab source, not an audit of the other cluster.

This is the operator-supplied topology in the other cluster. Services run in containers, but libvirt owns QEMU in host cgroups and OVN supplies guest networking. Do not infer a particular release, storage backend or floating-IP mode.

Kubernetes owns intent, manager owns the local QEMU process, and separate anchors give guest NICs independent Cilium identities. Node/storage helpers remain separately privileged. Image and volume scope is not yet a complete OpenStack product replacement.

slides.title: Where each VM boundary belongs
slides.subtitle: Engineering architecture review / code and ownership
slides.notes: Fifteen-minute technical narrative. Use the source register, capability ledger and detailed diagram catalog as the review appendix.

This is the operator-supplied topology in the other cluster. Services run in containers, but libvirt owns QEMU in host cgroups and OVN supplies guest networking. Do not infer a particular release, storage backend or floating-IP mode.

Kubernetes owns intent, manager owns the local QEMU process, and separate anchors give guest NICs independent Cilium identities. Node/storage helpers remain separately privileged. Image and volume scope is not yet a complete OpenStack product replacement.

slides.title: Remove services; assign the surviving work
slides.notes: These are responsibility mappings, not compatible APIs. Nova has more duties than issuing local hypervisor commands. Network address, routing and policy work survives removal of OVN. Image and volume requirements must be accepted explicitly.

slides.title: The code spine follows the ownership split
slides.notes: The workspace has 19 crates, 18 in the default path. Crate dependencies do not grant runtime authority: BMC/Redfish reuse manager abstractions while manager remains the private QMP owner.
Direct supervision aligns QEMU with its VM-specific container lifecycle and resource accounting. Process cleanup retains state authority through child reaping.

slides.title: A private QMP owner; a bounded public operation
points: Manager owns private QMP, QGA and VNC sessions.
BMC/Redfish authorize users before local control operations.
Protocol crates stay independent of Kubernetes, launchers, KVM and guest downloads.
slides.notes: The local socket trusts authorized same-UID peers. It is not another human login boundary or a generic remote QMP endpoint. Standalone embedded control is a separate deployment mode of the same abstraction.

A single Cilium fabric preserves separate management and NIC endpoint identities. The guest never shares the management network namespace. Each NIC costs a Pod/endpoint and requires explicit address/route ownership.

slides.title: One datapath still needs explicit control
points: Operator claims stable /32s and writes scoped FRR intent.
netd grants only authorized TAP/vhost descriptors.
Cilium policies enforce groups; labels alone do not create default deny.
slides.notes: Cilium BGP is a distinct upstream capability. Inspected qrab code uses frr-k8s. Ordinary attachment uses Cilium; duplicate-address live handoff depends on the local fork.

The target initiates the main connection, while bulk state moves source to target. Managers transfer supported VM state and switch control. Node peers transfer scoped conntrack. Shared disks are not copied. Guest-packet forwarding is another stream.

slides.title: A migration is an ownership transfer
points: Prepare a compatible target with empty identity state and fenced NICs.
Switch endpoint authority in the final pause; then adopt the exact target.
Refuse unsupported management state or auxiliary claims before unsafe side effects.
slides.notes: Powered-off VMs do not live-migrate, and the protocol is within qrab. Source completion, target adoption, forwarding grace and storage ownership must agree. No general cold-move/node-evacuation product is established.

slides.title: Three questions; three policy owners
rows: Kubernetes RBAC/admission or VM app roles
slides.notes: Kubernetes API authentication does not automatically authorize Redfish. A dashboard SVID is not a human console-admin grant. Guest workload identity and CHAP exports have additional distinct scopes.

The operator orchestrates scoped storage verbs through a separately authorized service. The root helper owns ZFS/LIO exports and fences. QEMU opens its own CHAP-authorized disk session; identity state uses another volume.

slides.title: Operate the boundaries
slides.subtitle: Failure-first workshop / qrab and OpenStack
slides.notes: Twenty-minute workshop. Ask who owns the state, what fresh evidence exists, and what could still be active before proposing a repair.

slides.title: A symptom is not the owner
rows: Guest is off; console still reachable
Manager power state versus Pod lifecycle
Guest packets fail; VM probes pass
New disk operation fails; guest I/O works
Storage control API versus data connection
The finalizer that still owns cleanup
slides.notes: Existing QEMU, kernel queue FDs and disk sessions can have different lifetimes from their control services. Read the exact VM/Pod/anchor/export identities before acting.

slides.title: Scenario: the old node vanished
points: Identify the exact old VM/Pod UID and disk generation.
Keep unknown writer ownership visible.
Require clean release or a completed backend fence before replacement.
slides.notes: A node lease, NotReady condition, missing API object or forced deletion is not a storage fence. Hand-declared disks retain the documented explicit administrator recovery.

Use this diagram to separate storage API failure from iSCSI data-path failure. CHAP authorizes access but does not enforce one writer or encrypt the payload. Native transport encryption has its own verified segment.

Two VM Pods during a migration are not automatically split brain: the target is prepared/fenced and ownership must transfer through the protocol. Conversely, API object names alone do not prove a safe transfer.

slides.title: Scenario: the user logs in but cannot act
points: Distinguish valid human identity from VM action role.
Check exact service SVID admission independently.
Check API RBAC/admission only for the declarative API path.
slides.notes: Do not validate a user issue with an unrelated cluster-admin or service credential and call the original user path proven. The dashboard is a trusted ServiceAccount deputy.

slides.title: Deletion is not one operation
slides.notes: The audit tightened PVC and access-group provenance. Source now supports a seven-day root guest-disk reaper; that does not establish installed state or cover Released state PVs automatically.

slides.title: After a fix, prove the invariant
points: Power cycle: expected new child PIDs, same intended identity.
Migration: exact adopted target, stable NIC identities and no unintended active source.
Recovery: old writer cannot act; credentials/export generation are correct.
slides.notes: A successful API response alone does not prove guest application health, traffic continuity, disk consistency or cleanup completeness. Use the maintained focused checks for the actual affected path.

slides.title: Release and evidence boundaries
points: Source merge is separate from image publication.
Digest pin / identity enrollment is separate from rollout.
A dated live record describes its named versions and scope.
slides.notes: Do not automatically apply example VM bundles or recreate deleted test VMs. Operational notes and work evidence belong in qrab towl.

slides.title: Workload cutover checklist
points: Boot + firmware + identity + management access.
Data consistency + backup/restore + one-writer recovery.
Network policy/routes/DNS + observation + data-aware rollback.
slides.notes: The other OpenStack cluster must supply its actual workload/backend inventory. No transparent OpenStack-to-qrab live migration or universal feature parity is assumed.

slides.title: One fabric, separate guest identities
slides.subtitle: Network review / OpenStack and qrab
slides.notes: The other OpenStack cluster is the supplied baseline. This is a responsibility and source comparison, not a direct inventory or performance measurement.
OpenStack uses Cilium for Kubernetes and OVN for guests in the supplied topology. qrab reuses Cilium for per-NIC endpoints while preserving separate management identity.
TAP/vhost kernel queues carry payload through the anchor namespace. The Unix socket grants descriptors and does not relay these packets.

slides.title: One fabric does not mean one identity

cards.title: Management Pod
cards.body: BMC / Redfish and private management listeners have the VM Pod endpoint.

cards.title: Guest NIC
cards.body: Each anchor has its own address, Cilium endpoint and security-group labels.

cards.title: Optional VPN NIC
cards.body: An anchor can route through its own tunnel and preserve its own policy scope.

slides.notes: Do not merge management loopback and guest traffic into one namespace. VPN-specific policy governs the anchor tunnel; it is optional.

slides.title: Network control still has explicit owners
points: Operator: stable address claims, anchor lifecycle, policy labels and scoped route intent.
netd: local TAP/vhost grants, routing, DHCP compatibility and handoff control.
Cilium + FRR: endpoint policy/datapath and BGP reachability, respectively.
slides.notes: A label alone is not a security group firewall. Unselected anchors follow the platform policy mode. Replacing Neutron removes its control plane after the required functions have owners.
Original peer liveness and held resource references supplement this simple identity view; see authority.md and A05/A06. Host scope names cannot establish Pod authority.

slides.title: Recover the namespace, not just the API name
points: A Pod UID can survive a CRI sandbox replacement.
A new held namespace changes the opaque attachment token and restarts bound DHCP.
Manager releases old queues before fresh attachment, preserving MAC and root port.
slides.notes: A07 includes real isolated namespace/FD lifetime tests and manager QMP ordering. Guest hot-unplug cooperation is required. Same-namespace netd restart retains the token.
VM state, switch control, node conntrack and guest packet forwarding are different streams. A local Cilium fork supports the duplicate-IP handoff contract.

slides.title: Three different migration concerns

cards.title: Endpoint authority
cards.body: Prepared target stays fenced until the controlled ownership switch.

cards.title: Connection state
cards.body: Node-bound authenticated peers copy only the scoped conntrack entries.

cards.title: Reachability
cards.body: FRR convergence and temporary forwarding have their own observations.

slides.notes: These are independent mechanisms; a BGP session or completed RAM transfer does not prove every flow survived.

slides.title: Distinguish a control outage from a payload fault
rows: netd socket, current anchor token, authorization and holder checks
Anchor routes, Cilium policy/endpoint, traffic origin and FRR paths
VM Pod endpoint and user/service admission
slides.notes: Existing queue descriptors may outlive netd. The source-derived expectation is not an availability guarantee.
Local kernel fixtures use stand-in uplinks, not Cilium. The two VPN fixtures were skipped without tools in the recorded run; never count early returns as datapath acceptance.

slides.title: Prove the selected workload network contract
points: Test allowed and denied guest paths separately from management access.
Observe address ownership, DNS, route convergence and recovery on the chosen release.
Exercise guest hot-unplug, migration and node-loss behavior with application evidence.
slides.notes: Desired acceptance criteria; source, manifest and local fixture evidence do not perform them.

slides.title: Images and disks: keep every surviving contract
slides.subtitle: Storage review / Glance and Cinder replacement
slides.notes: The other cluster storage backend was not supplied. Compare service responsibilities and qrab implementation, not invented backend topology.
Provisioning authority and guest disk I/O are separate. The small firmware/vTPM state filesystem is also separate from the guest LUN.

slides.title: Replace APIs; preserve required work
rows: BaseImage controller, verified import Jobs and sealed storage generations
Disk reconciler, scoped storage verbs, LIO/ZFS and export generations
Required catalog, backup/restore, recovery and operational subset
slides.notes: Existing foundations are substantial. No Glance/Cinder API compatibility, every backend or full feature parity is claimed.
Inspect and write Jobs receive constrained inputs. The controller owns the stage/seal lifecycle and records the verified generation.
The top-level digest cannot authenticate an extra backing file or external data file selected by metadata. Both Job modes reject dependencies before qemu-img.

slides.title: Image integrity has a precise boundary
points: Verify one downloaded source; reject undeclared backing and external-data inputs.
Let pinned QEMU perform full format validation and conversion.
Seal the verified raw generation; prepare backing chains in a trusted source environment.
slides.notes: The explicit fixture uses harmless local marker files and QEMU 11.1.3. It is not a live storage/import rollout test.

slides.title: Three resources with different ownership
rows: Export generation, CHAP and hard backend fencing
VM-bound identity lease and storage attachment contract
Verified source, sealed origin and clone/retirement contract
slides.notes: A state PVC is not the guest root disk. A local state lease is not hard storage fencing.

slides.title: One writer requires backend evidence

cards.title: Authenticate
cards.body: CHAP authorizes the exact export generation.

cards.title: Exclude old writers
cards.body: Clean ownership evidence or a completed hard backend fence gates replacement.

cards.title: Recover deliberately
cards.body: Unknown ownership stays unknown until the responsible storage barrier completes.

slides.notes: Pod deletion, NotReady and a lease timeout alone do not establish that an old writer cannot act.
Manager moves VM execution/identity state; shared guest disk blocks remain in the storage data path. This does not implement OpenStack-to-qrab live migration.

slides.title: Deletion is a staged storage lifecycle
points: Fence guest exports before releasing or retiring their ownership.
Native guest-disk destruction follows the separate grace reaper contract.
Retained identity PVC/PV cleanup and external access-group cleanup have other owners.
slides.notes: Independent source 0301347 adds the seven-day root guest-disk reaper. Its presence in source does not prove installed timer state or cover Released identity PVs.
Hermetic storage host tests do not exercise real ZFS/LIO drains. Real backend, recovery and backup acceptance remain separate.

slides.title: Finish the workload subset before retiring services
points: Prove import, clone, grow, attach and failure recovery on the chosen backend.
Prove application consistency and backup/restore, including retained identity state.
Record explicit destruction policy and a data-aware rollback procedure.
slides.notes: Desired acceptance; scope it from real workload requirements and the other cluster inventory.

slides.title: One login is not universal authority
slides.subtitle: Identity review / Keystone replacement
slides.notes: Kubernetes API auth, application user roles, workload identity, guest identity and storage credentials have separate enforcement owners.
Use the question first: human subject, action grant, calling service, guest workload or disk export. Do not treat OIDC and SPIFFE as interchangeable.

slides.title: Keystone leaves; these owners remain
rows: May this API request change a VM?
May this human manage this VM?
Verified OIDC identity and the application VM role
Is this the allowed calling service?
Exact workload SPIFFE identity and rotating mTLS
slides.notes: The dashboard backend uses its ServiceAccount; it is not per-user Kubernetes impersonation. Application authorization remains explicit.
Workload admission does not grant the human action. Both gates apply on the workload management route; development/native credential entrypoints have their own documented scope.

slides.title: A management action crosses explicit gates
points: Dashboard checks the selected VM and keeps the human bearer server-side.
The VM service admits the exact workload peer and verifies the human action role.
Manager receives a bounded local operation and retains its private QMP authority.
slides.notes: Service discovery must resolve only the selected immutable VM destination. A successful TLS handshake is not a power/console authorization result.

slides.title: Console access has its own path and role
points: Graphical console admission is admin-scoped.
Private VNC is reached through authenticated, selected-VM proxy hops.
Guest packet identities remain in separate NIC anchors.
slides.notes: A guest does not share the VM management loopback listeners. The diagram portfolio has the full console chain.

slides.title: Guest identity is optional and VM-bound
points: Software-TPM credentials bind the intended VM identity lifecycle.
The relay carries opaque agent/server TLS bytes rather than issuing identities.
Software vTPM does not provide confidential-computing isolation from the node.
slides.notes: Retired SVSM/confidential-computing work is archived. Guest SPIRE enrollment and a host service SVID are distinct credentials.

slides.title: Cleanup follows lifecycle provenance
rows: Exact launch/VM/claim provenance or established owner
Recorded created UUIDs and exact generated names
Authorize actions; do not redefine old cleanup ownership
slides.notes: A01/A02 cover failing-before regressions. Public annotations are provenance under trusted API writers, not cryptographic attestations.
Identity configuration, successful service admission and a real user-role operation are different observations. Record expiry/rotation/recovery behavior explicitly.

slides.title: Review the remaining trust contract
points: Assign trusted namespace/API writers and required tenant isolation.
Prove issuer/audience/role scope, exact service peers and credential rotation.
Keep human login, guest workload identity and disk fencing as distinct decisions.
slides.notes: Desired acceptance criteria. Removing Keystone does not automatically implement all of them.
